title: May Not Even a Thorn Pierce • The Seventy Qurra’ • A Month of Invoking Curses

blocks.0: May Not Even a Thorn Pierce
blocks.1: Safwan ibn Umayyah bought Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah (RA), to take revenge for his father. He took him to al-Tan‘im to kill him. A group of people of Makkah gathered to watch, Abu Sufyan among them. Abu Sufyan stood before Zayd (RA) and said, tell me in Allah’s name, Zayd (RA), would you like Muhammad to be in your place now, we cut his neck, and you sit with your family?
blocks.3: By Allah, I would not want Muhammad, in his place, to have even a small thorn prick his foot, while I sit among my family.{{1}}
blocks.4: Abu Sufyan later used to say, I have not seen anyone among people with a love like the love of Muhammad’s Companions for him.{{1}}
blocks.5: Then Zayd (RA) was killed. Khubayb (RA) and Zayd (RA) were martyred on the same day. The Prophet {{1}} had said that day, peace be upon you, Khubayb (RA), Quraysh has killed you.{{2}}
blocks.6: His life was going, yet there was not a word from Zayd’s (RA) mouth for himself. Only one thought, that not even a thorn should touch the Prophet’s {{1}} foot. When we fall into hardship we think first of ourselves. Those who have truly loved think of the safety of the beloved even in their own last moment. The hypocrites were then saying, what did these people get? They neither stayed in their homes, nor could they get the news to the Prophet. Allah revealed verses in answer to them.
blocks.8: And among people there is one whose words about worldly life please you, and he calls Allah to witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the most hostile of (your) enemies.{{1}}
blocks.10: And (on the other hand) among people there is one who sells his own life to seek the pleasure of Allah. Allah is most compassionate to (such) servants.{{1}}
blocks.11: The same event, two kinds of eyes. In the hypocrite’s eyes, failure; in Allah’s eyes, a life sold, whose price is Allah’s pleasure.{{1}}
blocks.13: A few months after Raji‘ the second group also set out. At the request of Abu Bara’ ‘Amir ibn Malik. Abu Bara’ himself had come to Madinah. He had not become Muslim on hearing about Islam, nor gone far away. He had said, if you send some Companions to the people of Najd, call them, I hope they will respond. The Prophet {{1}} had said, I fear the people of Najd will harm them. Abu Bara’ had said, I am their guarantor.{{2}}
blocks.14: The Prophet {{1}} made Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA) the leader of this group.
blocks.16: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} sent seventy men known as the Qurra’ to help against an enemy. By day they gathered firewood, by night they prayed. When they reached Bi’r Ma‘unah, they were killed, treacherously.{{2}}
blocks.17: Reaching Bi’r Ma‘unah they sent the Prophet’s {{1}} letter to ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl, the nephew of Abu Bara’, in the hand of Haram ibn Milhan (RA), the maternal uncle of Anas (RA). ‘Amir did not even look at the letter; he pounced and killed him at once.{{2}}
blocks.18: At the moment of death Haram (RA) took his own blood in his hand, sprinkled it over his face and head, and said,
blocks.20: I have won, by the Lord of the Ka‘bah.{{1}}
blocks.21: The one being killed says, I have won. Because his reckoning was of the Hereafter, not of the world. A man of ‘Amir’s force later asked, what does ‘I have won’ mean? He was told, Paradise. He said, indeed so. That very day he accepted Islam.{{1}}
blocks.22: Then ‘Amir called the tribe of Banu ‘Amir for help. They said, we will not break Abu Bara’’s promise. ‘Amir then called some clans of Banu Sulaym, Ri‘l, Dhakwan, ‘Usayyah. They agreed. They came and surrounded the remaining Companions. Everyone fought with swords in hand, in the end everyone was martyred. Except one, Ka‘b ibn Zayd, who was left wounded, thought dead. He survived, and was later martyred in the Battle of the Trench.{{1}}
blocks.23: The very words whose meaning Haram (RA) himself understood best at the moment of speaking them later drew even an enemy to the path of Islam. The herd of camels was being grazed away from the camp that day, as every day, to feed on grass; in charge of that herd were ‘Amr ibn Umayyah (RA) and an Ansari Companion of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. Because they were away from the camp they survived the attack. Seeing a flock of vultures circling over the camp, they sensed something had happened. Going near, they saw their companions all lying in blood. The Ansari Companion asked, what is your view? ‘Amr (RA) said, let us go to the Prophet {{1}} and tell him. The Ansari Companion said, I will not move from the place where Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA) was martyred; let people never be able to say that I left him alone and ran away. He fought, in the end he was martyred. One was given the chance to leave safely. He refused that chance, because leaving the place of his leader’s martyrdom was, to him, the real danger. Of the chances we seize to avoid trouble, is each one truly safety, or another form of shame? ‘Amr (RA) was taken captive. When he gave his tribe’s name, ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl let him go, in place of one vow of his mother.{{2}}
blocks.24: In that group was ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA), the freed slave of Abu Bakr (RA). He too was killed.
blocks.26: When they were martyred at Bi’r Ma‘unah and ‘Amr ibn Umayyah (RA) was taken captive, ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl pointed to one of the slain and asked ‘Amr, who is this? ‘Amr said, this is ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA). ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl said, I saw that after he was killed he was raised toward the sky, until I could see him between the sky and the earth, then he was laid down on the ground.{{1}}
blocks.27: The news reached Madinah. The Prophet {{1}} announced their martyrdom, saying, your companions were attacked, and they asked their Lord, our Lord, inform our brothers that we are pleased with You and You are pleased with us. The names of ‘Urwah ibn Zubayr and Mundhir ibn Zubayr were later given after ‘Urwah ibn Asma’ and Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA), who were martyred that day.{{2}}
blocks.29: On getting the news the Prophet {{1}} was heartbroken. Such grief had not been seen even after Uhud.
blocks.31: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} for a month recited qunut after rising from ruku‘, invoking a curse in the names of some Arab tribes. This was the beginning of qunut, before this we did not recite qunut.{{2}}
blocks.32: Those tribes were Ri‘l, Dhakwan, ‘Usayyah and Banu Lihyan, who had betrayed at Raji‘ and Bi’r Ma‘unah. One month. Every day. The same words. When grief runs so deep, even then the Prophet {{1}} chose the path of du‘a, not of the sword. He did not send an army to take revenge, he only asked of Allah. However, Banu Lihyan’s account was not entirely settled; about two years later there was an expedition against them, that story is for a later dars.{{2}}
blocks.33: Anas (RA) used to say, a verse was revealed about these martyrs, we used to recite it, later it was lifted. Its meaning was: tell our people that we have met our Lord, He is pleased with us, and we are pleased with Him.{{1}}

quiz.q: What question did Abu Sufyan ask Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah?
o: Do you want to abandon Islam and save your life
Where is your family now
Whether he wanted Muhammad in his place or not
Why were you really captured

quiz.q: What was the gist of Zayd’s famous answer?
o: If you free me now I will go straight home to Madinah
I do not actually know Muhammad
I will never forgive you
I do not want even a thorn to prick Muhammad’s foot

quiz.q: Why did Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah use the image of ‘a thorn’ in his answer?
o: Even the slightest pain of the Prophet ﷺ weighed more to him than his own death
He was truly suffering sharply from a thorn wound at that moment
A desire to insult Abu Sufyan in the course of the talk
A trick to waste time because he did not know the answer

quiz.q: What question does Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah’s answer teach us to ask today?
o: Whether it is right to expect a return for love
Whether it is even right to talk with an enemy
Whether fear of death is a natural reaction
How deep my own love for the Prophet ﷺ really is

quiz.q: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, how many Companions were sent to Bi’r Ma‘unah?
o: Seventy
Forty
Sixty
One hundred

quiz.q: What did Haram ibn Milhan (RA) say when speared?
o: Allahu Akbar
Fuztu wa Rabb al-Ka‘bah (I have won, by the Lord of the Ka‘bah)
La ilaha illa Allah
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un (we belong to Allah and to Him we return)

quiz.q: After the killing of ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA), what is narrated to have been seen?
o: Light came out of his grave
His blood turned white
His body was raised toward the sky
It is narrated that the smile never left his face

quiz.q: At Bi’r Ma‘unah, what is the difference between Abu Bara’’s (RA) promise and ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl’s act?
o: Both were considered to have given equal full protection in the end
One gave protection, the other himself broke that protection
Both took part together in the betrayal
Abu Bara’ had not made any promise at all

quiz.q: What aspect of the Companions’ way of life shows in their being called ‘Qurra’’?
o: They were attentive all the time only to memorizing the Qur’an
They kept away from all kinds of war
Carrying on together the day’s labour and the night’s long worship
They were people of Madinah’s richest families

quiz.q: What realization shows in Haram ibn Milhan’s (RA) saying ‘fuztu’ (I have won)?
o: Losing consciousness at the moment of intense pain
An attempt to temporarily confuse the enemy
A tactic to keep up the morale of companions behind
Regarding martyrdom not as defeat but as real success

quiz.q: What balance does the ‘Qurra’’ identity of the Bi’r Ma‘unah Companions recall in today’s busy life?
o: Dividing time between livelihood and worship
One should abandon livelihood entirely for worship
One should give all one’s time only to livelihood
Sleep at night is the most important thing in life

quiz.q: How can Haram ibn Milhan’s (RA) ‘fuztu’ change our thinking about death today?
o: Pretending not to fear death at the moment of danger
Learning to regard success in the Hereafter as the real success of life
Forcing a smiling face in every calamity is obligatory
It is better to avoid thinking of death as much as possible

quiz.q: For how long did the Prophet ﷺ invoke curses in qunut against the traitors of Raji‘ and Bi’r Ma‘unah?
o: One week
Three days
Forty days
One month

quiz.q: What was the meaning of the verse revealed about the martyrs of Bi’r Ma‘unah that was later abrogated?
o: We have met our Lord, He is pleased, and we are pleased
Allah has forgiven us and given us a high rank in Paradise
Revenge for our killing will soon be taken
We are not really martyrs, we are still alive

quiz.q: What is understood from the Prophet’s ﷺ invoking curses in qunut for a month?
o: Feeling the pain of betrayal for a long time
Repeatedly failing for a time to control anger
Some new event happening every day
The rules of qunut not yet being settled then

quiz.q: What is understood from the recitation of the verse revealed about the martyrs later being abrogated?
o: It was later proved that this whole event was not actually true
Even if the recitation of some parts of the Qur’an is abrogated, the meaning and rank remain intact
The rank of the martyrs was later reduced
The Companions had forgotten to memorize the verse

quiz.q: The Prophet’s ﷺ invoking curses in qunut for a month recalls which deed for us today?
o: Setting out in anger to take revenge on one’s own
Thinking that making du‘a just once is enough
Being regular and continuous in du‘a against injustice
Only patiently staying silent without making du‘a
